feature: A walk whose app died says the app died
summary: When a scripted walk ends because the app crashed, the run now says so and names the frames it died in, instead of printing the same 'no done.json' a merely slow walk prints. It also ends in about nine seconds instead of sitting out the full three minute timeout.
setup: A terminal in the repo. Nothing to install, nothing in the app to turn on. The probe bundle is already built; every command below is safe to run while you are using the dev app.

try.note: Every line says ok. This is the reader of macOS crash reports, drilled against the real rename crash of 2026-09-17 night.

The first line is what a sweep would print: EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT) in EditorState.document.getter < EditorState.readWordsForRows.getter < closure #1 in EditorState.renameLayer(id:to:). Read < as 'called from'.
Both pass in twelve seconds and nothing mentions a crash, because the app no longer crashes. The picture is the window this walk photographed at step 13.

try.do: Put the crash back for one run: git stash && git checkout 6bfe4969^ -- Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift Sources/PhotonzCore/History.swift && Scripts/build-app.sh --probe
try.note: Two minutes of building. This is the only way to see a real crash, since the bug is fixed.
unique-layer-names-walk now reads CRASHED with the frames, the summary reads '1 passed, 0 failed, 1 crashed', and the whole thing takes nineteen seconds where it used to take 187.

try.do: Put it back: git checkout HEAD -- Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift Sources/PhotonzCore/History.swift && Scripts/build-app.sh --probe && git stash pop
Prove a slow walk still reads as slow: PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST_TIMEOUT=1 Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build experiments-groups
try.note: It says 'ran out of time after 1s, with the app still running', which is a different sentence from a crash and is meant to stay that way.

evaluate: Reading only the walk's one line, can you tell a crash from a slow walk without opening anything else?

Is the frame list the right length: does 'EditorState.document.getter < EditorState.readWordsForRows.getter < closure #1 in EditorState.renameLayer(id:to:)' tell you where to look, or would one frame have done?

When macOS skips a repeat crash report, the line says 'no report of its own; the crash 77s earlier was ...'. Is that the right amount of doubt, or should a crash with no report of its own say only that the app died?
A crash still costs about ten seconds waiting for macOS to write the report. Is that worth it for the frames, or should the walk give up sooner and say less?
Should a sweep stop dead at the first crash instead of running the other 300 walks against an app that has just proved it can die?
rough: macOS writes one crash report per crash signature and then skips repeats: two runs of the same crashing walk 18 seconds apart left one report between them. The second walk says 'no report of its own; the crash 18s earlier was ...' and shows that report's frames, which are the likely shape of the crash rather than proof of it.
A walk's output folder is never cleared between runs, so a walk that crashed at step 17 still has the pictures an earlier passing run left at steps 25 and 31 sitting beside it. Filed as its own task.

The standing failing-walks task now carries a crash section naming what each one died in, but that path has only been proved by drill, not by a real sweep that crashed. The next sweep with a crash in it is the first real reading.

A crash is still counted as a failure for everything downstream, so a sweep with one crash and no other failure exits 1 and files the walk in the usual list. That seems right, but it does mean a crash does not interrupt the sweep in any way.
